hardware_summary: On-site gas turbine drivers mechanically driving the refrigerant compressors of the (shelved) Lake Charles Liquefaction export trains; no on-site electricity generation -- facility electrical load is grid-fed via a new Entergy 230-kV line, with diesel-only standby gensets for emergency backup (fuel gate fails for the backup units, not the mechanical-drive turbines).
fuel_basis: FERC/DOE Final EIS (EIS-0491, Aug 2015) describes a "fuel gas system to provide high-pressure gas to the refrigerant gas turbine drivers" -- confirms the compressor-driving turbines are gas-fired.
captive_summary: The Lake Charles Liquefaction export-train design (shelved) uses on-site gas turbines to mechanically drive the mixed-refrigerant compressors directly (shaft power, no generator) -- a mechanical-drive captive gas power arrangement. The project's own alternatives analysis explicitly considered and rejected both (a) electric-motor-driven compressors (would require >800 MW of grid electric supply) and (b) a dedicated on-site power-generation plant (single- or combined-cycle) to supply that electric-motor option, confirming the as-designed configuration is direct gas-turbine mechanical drive, not electric generation. Facility electrical (non-compression) load is supplied by a new ~19-mile 230-kV Entergy transmission line; four 4,000-kW diesel-only standby generators provide emergency backup (diesel fails the fuel gate and does not count).
mechanical_drive_note: Gas turbine drivers powering the refrigerant compressors of the liquefaction trains (FEIS section on fuel gas / turbine drivers); exact turbine count/model/aggregate MW rating not stated in the passages reviewed, though the rejected electric-motor alternative was quantified at over 800 MW of equivalent electric load, indicating large aggregate shaft power.
confirmed_how: FERC/DOE Final Environmental Impact Statement for the Lake Charles Liquefaction Project (EIS-0491, Aug 2015, prepared for Trunkline LNG Company / Lake Charles LNG Export Company, an Energy Transfer affiliate): (1) states the fuel gas system supplies "the refrigerant gas turbine drivers"; (2) describes the Entergy 230-kV line and four 4,000-kW diesel stand-by generators for facility electrical needs / backup; (3) section 3.7 'Alternative Power Sources' states electric-motor-driven compressors were "ruled out at the time due to the excessive amount of electrical power required (above 800 megawatts)" and that "on-site power generation by both single- and combined-cycle plants was ruled out in the design of the Lake Charles Liquefaction Project" -- confirming the built/approved design relies on direct gas-turbine mechanical drive, not electric generation.
